title: pinout-asyncapi consumed-contract (consumer-side input artifact)
description: The consumer's captured usage of a provider: which channels it talks on, and per direction which message fields it actually SENDS and READS — typed from the provider spec at capture time — plus a provenance stamp. Produced by the E-harness `component-tests` skill from the consumer's stubs and tests; consumed by `pinout-asyncapi validate` via config.consumer.consumed_contract_path. This is NOT an AsyncAPI document and NOT a raw stub: it is a schema-shaped projection. Owned by pinout-asyncapi because the async form (channel x direction) does not follow from the sync twin's form (path+method). FROZEN: this is the consumer-side input contract of the service.

consumer.description: Consumer service name. Must equal config.consumer.name; mismatch -> PARSE_ERROR (exit 3).

provenance.description: Which provider spec this contract was captured from. Echoed verbatim into report.provenance so pinout-netlist can track freshness and re-check when the provider changes. Stamped at generation time — never hand-written.

provider_version.description: Version stamp of the source spec (AsyncAPI info.version or the commit that produced it).

captured_hash.description: sha256 of the captured provider spec bytes.

channels.description: One entry per channel the consumer talks on. Every address listed in config.consumer.channels must appear here.

channel.description: A channel the consumer uses. At least one of `sends` / `receives` must be non-empty — a channel with neither direction is meaningless and is a CONFIG-side defect of the generator. The communication pattern is DERIVED, never declared: sends+receives = request-reply (rule R9 applies per message), sends only = fire-and-forget, receives only = publish-subscribe (docs/concept.md §2).

address.description: Channel identity: the AsyncAPI `channel.address` of the provider channel, or the channel key when the spec omits `address`. Matched against the provider spec by rule R1.

protocol.description: Transport protocol as captured from the provider's `channel.servers -> server.protocol`, e.g. `kafka`, `amqp`, `mqtt`, `ws`, `ibmmq`, `http`. Compared by rule R2: a kafka topic and an amqp queue at the same address are not the same channel.

sends.description: Messages the consumer PUBLISHES to this channel. Checked CONTRAVARIANTLY against the provider's `action: receive` operation on the same channel: required(provider) subset-of fields(sends) — rule R5.

receives.description: Messages the consumer CONSUMES from this channel. Checked COVARIANTLY against the provider's `action: send` operation on the same channel: fields(receives) subset-of properties(provider) — rule R6. This is the direction that catches provider field removal.

message.description: One message on one direction of one channel.

name.description: Pairing key: the key of this message in the provider CHANNEL's `messages` map (e.g. `getBalanceRequest`), NOT the message `name` field and NOT the components.messages key. Rationale: the parser overwrites Message.Name with a codegen identifier during Process(), so the map key is the only stable spec-authored identifier (docs/concept.md D8). Consumer names a message absent from the provider direction -> MESSAGE_NOT_IN_PROVIDER (rule R4). Printed in report `location`.

content_type.description: Effective content type at capture time (message.contentType, else the spec's defaultContentType). Compared by rule R8, and ONLY when the consumer declares it: a provider content type the consumer never pinned is not a violation. Absent here -> not checked.

correlation_id_location.description: Runtime expression of the AsyncAPI `correlationId.location`, e.g. `$message.header#/correlationId`. Compared by rule R9, and ONLY when the consumer declares it (the consumer actually correlates); then the provider message must declare an equal `correlationId.location`. Absent here -> not checked, because a provider correlationId the consumer ignores is a legal superset. NOT gated on the communication pattern: AsyncAPI 3.0 request-reply usually spans two different channel addresses, so a per-channel both-directions test would never fire (docs/concept.md D9).

payload.description: The message body surface the consumer actually uses: for `sends` — the fields it populates; for `receives` — the fields it reads. Not the provider's full schema.

headers.description: The message header surface the consumer actually uses. Compared by exactly the same rules as `payload`.

schema.description: Captured field surface — a deliberately small subset of JSON Schema. NOTE the absence of `required`: a consumed-contract states what the consumer SENDS and READS, not what it demands. `properties` IS the used-field set, and that set is what rules R5/R6 compare; types come from the provider spec at capture time and feed rule R7. Adding `required` here would create a field no rule reads.

type.description: JSON Schema type. Compared by rule R7.

format.description: JSON Schema format as typed from the provider spec, e.g. `int64`, `date-time`. Compared by rule R7 alongside `type`.

enum.description: Captured enum values, when the provider field was an enum. Informational in MVP — not compared (docs/concept.md §6).

properties.description: Used fields of an object, recursively. Present when type == object.

items.description: Element schema of an array, recursively. Present when type == array.
